RestrictStartDate="2026-09-14"><Primary><Schedules RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2025-11-01"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" NumberOfProvisions="32" id="schedule-15" RestrictExtent="E+W+S" RestrictStartDate="2025-11-01"><Number>
		SCHEDULE 15</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Consequential and Minor Amendments of Enactments</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air" NumberOfProvisions="1" RestrictExtent="E+W+S" id="schedule-15-crossheading-workplace-emissions-into-the-air" RestrictStartDate="2015-02-26"><Title> Workplace emissions into the air</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14" RestrictExtent="E+W+S" RestrictStartDate="2015-02-26" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14"><Pnumber><CommentaryRef Ref="key-9fdf82"/>14</Pnumber><P1para><Text>. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .</Text></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43" NumberOfProvisions="402" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Primary xmlns:leg="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation"><Schedules><Title>SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" NumberOfProvisions="35" NumberFormat="default" id="schedule-15"><Number>SCHEDULE 15</Number><TitleBlock>
<Title>Consequential and Minor Amendments of Enactments</Title>
</TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air" NumberOfProvisions="1" id="schedule-15-crossheading-workplace-emissions-into-the-air"><Title>Workplace emissions into the air</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14">
<Pnumber>14</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Section 5 of the <MarginNoteRef Ref="m00160"/>Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (general duty in relation to harmful emissions into the air from prescribed premises) shall be amended by the insertion—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/a/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/a" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in subsection (1), at the beginning, of the words “Subject to subsection (5) below,”; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/b/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/b" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>after subsection (4), of the following subsections—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" TargetClass="primary" Context="main" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The foregoing provisions of this section shall not apply in relation to any process which is a prescribed process as from the date which is the determination date for that process.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For the purposes of subsection (6) above, the “determination date” for a prescribed process is—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the case of a process for which an authorisation is granted, the date on which the enforcing authority grants it, whether in pursuance of the application or, on an appeal, of a direction to grant it;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the case of a process for which an authorisation is refused, the date of the refusal or, on an appeal, of the affirmation of the refusal.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsections (5) and (6) above “authorisation”, “enforcing authority” and “prescribed process” have the meaning given in section 1 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and the reference to an appeal is a reference to an appeal under section 15 of that Act.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P1para>
</P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

RestrictStartDate="2025-11-01"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" NumberOfProvisions="32" id="schedule-15" RestrictExtent="E+W+S" RestrictStartDate="2025-11-01"><Number>

<Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43" NumberOfProvisions="402" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0"><Primary xmlns:leg="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation"><Schedules><Title>SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15" NumberOfProvisions="35" NumberFormat="default" id="schedule-15"><Number>SCHEDULE 15</Number><TitleBlock>
<Title>Consequential and Minor Amendments of Enactments</Title>
</TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/crossheading/workplace-emissions-into-the-air" NumberOfProvisions="1" id="schedule-15-crossheading-workplace-emissions-into-the-air"><Title>Workplace emissions into the air</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14">
<Pnumber>14</Pnumber>
<P1para>
<Text>Section 5 of the <MarginNoteRef Ref="m00160"/>Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 (general duty in relation to harmful emissions into the air from prescribed premises) shall be amended by the insertion—</Text>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/a/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/a" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14-a">
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in subsection (1), at the beginning, of the words “Subject to subsection (5) below,”; and</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/b/enacted" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1990/43/schedule/15/paragraph/14/b" id="schedule-15-paragraph-14-b">
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>after subsection (4), of the following subsections—</Text>
<BlockAmendment TargetSubClass="unknown" TargetClass="primary" Context="main" Format="default" NumberFormat="default">
<P2>
<Pnumber>5</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>The foregoing provisions of this section shall not apply in relation to any process which is a prescribed process as from the date which is the determination date for that process.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>6</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>For the purposes of subsection (6) above, the “determination date” for a prescribed process is—</Text>
<P3>
<Pnumber>a</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the case of a process for which an authorisation is granted, the date on which the enforcing authority grants it, whether in pursuance of the application or, on an appeal, of a direction to grant it;</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
<P3>
<Pnumber>b</Pnumber>
<P3para>
<Text>in the case of a process for which an authorisation is refused, the date of the refusal or, on an appeal, of the affirmation of the refusal.</Text>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P2para>
</P2>
<P2>
<Pnumber>7</Pnumber>
<P2para>
<Text>In subsections (5) and (6) above “authorisation”, “enforcing authority” and “prescribed process” have the meaning given in section 1 of the Environmental Protection Act 1990 and the reference to an appeal is a reference to an appeal under section 15 of that Act.</Text>
</P2para>
</P2>
</BlockAmendment>
</P3para>
</P3>
</P1para>
</P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

RestrictStartDate="2014-04-22"><Primary><Body DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/body" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/body" NumberOfProvisions="11" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5" id="section-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/1" id="section-5-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For the purpose of enabling effect to be given to the 1992 Protocols, the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340821"/>Merchant Shipping (Oil Pollution) Act 1971 and the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340831"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1974 shall have effect subject to the amendments contained in Parts I and II respectively of Schedule 4 to the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340841"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1988 with the substitution, in the definition in section 19(1) of the1971 Act of “the Convention” and in the definitions in section 1(1) of the1974 Act of “the Liability Convention” and “the Fund Convention”, of “1992” for “1984”.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2" id="section-5-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Accordingly—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/a" id="section-5-2-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the word “<Term id="term-1984">1984</Term>” shall be omitted from the section 4A(1) of the 1974 Act and the paragraph 4(a) and (d) constituting Schedule 1 to the 1974 Act as respectively inserted and substituted by Part II of Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/2/b" id="section-5-2-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>paragraph 18 of Schedule 4 to the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340851"/>Merchant Shipping (Registration, <Abbreviation Expansion="et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc.</Abbreviation>) Act 1993 (which provides that section 34 of and Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act shall not have effect) is hereby repealed and the entry for Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act shall be deemed not to have been included in Part II of Schedule 5 to the 1993 Act (pre-consolidation repeals).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3" id="section-5-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Her Majesty may by Order in Council make such provision as appears to Her Majesty to be appropriate i n connection with the implementation of any transitional provisions contained in the 1992 Protocols or the Conventions which they amend; and any such Order may in particular provide, in relation to occurrences of any description specified in the Order—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a" id="section-5-3-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for provisions of the1971 Act or the1974 Act to have effect—</Text><P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/i" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/i" id="section-5-3-a-i"><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>to such extent as is so specified, as if Schedule 4 to the 1988 Act were not in force, and</Text></P4para></P4><P4 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/ii" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/a/ii" id="section-5-3-a-ii"><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>to such extent as is so specified, as if that Schedule were in force;</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/3/b" id="section-5-3-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for any such provisions to have effect (whether as amended by that Schedule or not) subject to such modifications as are so specified.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4" id="section-5-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this section “<Term id="term-the-1992-protocols">the 1992 Protocols</Term>” means—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/a" id="section-5-4-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the Protocol of 1992 to amend the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage 1969 signed in London on 27th November 1992; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/5/4/b" id="section-5-4-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the Protocol of 1992 to amend the International Convention on the Establishment of an International Fund for Compensation for Oil Pollution Damage 1971 signed in London on 27th November 1992.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

xmls: <Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28" NumberOfProvisions="78" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="1994-10-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Extension of rights of Fund by subrogation.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7" id="section-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1" id="section-7-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In section 8 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340891"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1974 (Acquisition by International Fund of rights of recipients of payments made by the Fund in cases of oil pollution damage)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/a" id="section-7-1-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for subsection (1), there shall be inserted the following subsection—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text> In respect of any sum paid by the Fund as compensation for pollution damage the Fund shall acquire by subrogation any rights in respect of the damage which the recipient has (or but for the payment would have) against any other person,</Text></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment><AppendText>; and</AppendText></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/1/b" id="section-7-1-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>subsection (3) shall be omitted.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/7/2" id="section-7-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The amendments made by subsection (1) above apply in relation to payments made by the Fund after this section comes into force.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

RestrictStartDate="1995-01-01" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" ConfersPower="true" Match="false"><Title> Power to implement 1990 OPRC Convention.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/2" id="section-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/2/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/2/1" id="section-2-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Section 20 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340791"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1979 (power by Order in Council to implement international conventions relating to pollution from ships, <Abbreviation Expansion="Et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc</Abbreviation>) shall have effect with the insertion in subsection (1), after paragraph (c), of the following paragraph—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P3><Pnumber>cc</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the International Convention on Oil Pollution Preparedness, Response and Co-operation, 1990 (including the Final Act of the Conference and the attached resolutions) signed in London on 30th November 1990;</Text></P3para></P3></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/2/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/2/2" id="section-2-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In consequence of the amendment made by subsection (1) above, in subsection (6) of that section for the words “(a) to (c)” there shall be substituted the words <InlineAmendment>“
              (a) to (cc)

RestrictStartDate="1994-07-28" RestrictEndDate="1996-01-01" Match="false"><Title> Amendments as to powers of implementation.</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3" id="section-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/1" id="section-3-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Section 20 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1979 (power by Order in Council to implement international conventions relating to pollution from ships, etc) shall be amended as follows.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/2" id="section-3-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (3)(a), in the list of enactments there specified, after the entry for the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8340801"/>Merchant Shipping Act 1970, there shall be inserted the following entry— <InlineAmendment>“
              section 33 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1988 (which relates to investigations of marine accidents);
            ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/3" id="section-3-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (4), after paragraph (a), there shall be inserted the following paragraph—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P3><Pnumber>aa</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make provision in terms of any document which the Secretary of State or any person considers relevant from time to time;</Text></P3para></P3></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1994/28/section/3/4" id="section-3-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After subsection (4), there shall be inserted the following subsections—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>4A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an Order in Council under subsection (1) of this section authorises the making of regulations for the purpose of giving effect to an agreement mentioned in paragraphs (a) to (cc) or falling within paragraph (d) of that subsection the Order also authorises the making of regulations for the purpose of giving effect to an agreement which provides for the modification of such an agreement.</Text></P2para><P2para><Text>This subsection applies in relation to Orders in Council and international agreements whenever made.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4B</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations made by virtue of paragraph (e) of subsection (4) of this section—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>may make provision corresponding to the provision authorised for an Order by paragraphs (a) to (d) of subsection (4) of this section; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>shall be subject to annulment in pursuance of a resolution of either House of Parliament.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></P1group></Pblock></Body></Primary></Legislation>

RestrictStartDate="2020-12-31"><Primary><Schedules RestrictStartDate="2020-12-31"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1" NumberOfProvisions="12" id="schedule-1" RestrictExtent="S" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01"><Number>SCHEDULE 1</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Setting and alteration of certain penalties</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/crossheading/increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/crossheading/increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences" NumberOfProvisions="1" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01" id="schedule-1-crossheading-increase-of-fines-for-certain-summary-offences"><Title> Increase of fines for certain summary offences</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3" RestrictStartDate="1996-04-01" BlanketAmendment="true" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/1" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The enactments specified in column 2 of Part II of Schedule 2 to this Act, which relate to the maximum fines for the offences mentioned (and broadly described) in column 1 of that Schedule, shall have effect as if the maximum fine that may be imposed on summary conviction of any offence so mentioned were a fine not exceeding the amount specified in column 4 of that Schedule instead of a fine not exceeding the amount specified in column 3 of that Schedule (being the amount of the maximum fine in respect of the offence immediately before the passing of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8315571"/>Criminal Law Act 1977), but this sub-paragraph shall not alter the maximum daily fine, if any, provided for by any of those enactments.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/2" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In section 203 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8315581"/>Local Government (Scotland) Act 1973 (offences against byelaws), except as applied to byelaws made under any provision contained in a local or private Act other than by a local authority, for any reference to £20 there shall be substituted a reference to £50.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subject to sub-paragraph (4) below, this sub-paragraph applies to any pre-1949 enactment however framed or worded which—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>as regards any summary offence makes a person liable on conviction thereof to a fine of, or not exceeding, a specified amount less than £50 which has not been altered since the end of 1948 (and is not altered by this Act); or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/3/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-3-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>confers power by subordinate instrument to make a person, as regards any summary offence (whether or not created by the instrument), liable on conviction thereof to a fine of, or a maximum fine of, less than £50 which has not been altered since the end of 1948 (and is not altered by this Act).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/4" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to any offence to which section 292(2)(b) of the Principal Act applies (offences triable only summarily other than by virtue of express provision).</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Every enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies shall have effect as if for the specified amount less than £50 there mentioned there were substituted—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>£25 if the specified amount is less than £20; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/5/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-5-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>£50 if the specified amount is not less than £20.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/6" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-6"><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where, by virtue of any enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies by virtue of sub-sub-paragraph (a) of that sub-paragraph, a person convicted of a summary offence would, apart from this paragraph, be liable to a fine, or maximum fine, of one amount in the case of a first conviction and of a different amount in the case of a second or subsequent conviction, sub-paragraph (5) above shall apply separately in relation to each specified amount less than £50, even if this produces the same instead of different amounts for different convictions.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/7" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Sub-paragraph (3) above does not apply to so much of any enactment as, in whatever words, makes a person liable or provides for a person to be made liable, on summary conviction, to a fine or a maximum fine for each period of a specified length during which a continuing offence is committed.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/8" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/8" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-8"><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Where an enactment to which sub-paragraph (3) above applies provides or confers a power to provide for, on conviction of an offence triable only summarily, a fine or a maximum fine in respect of a specified quantity or a specified number of things, “<Term id="term-the-specified-amount">the specified amount</Term>” for the purposes of subsection (5) above is the fine or maximum fine so provided or for which provision may be made.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/9" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/9" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-9"><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (3) above “<Term id="term-pre-1949-enactment">pre-1949 enactment</Term>” means an enactment passed before 1st January 1949 or an enactment passed on or after that date which whether directly or, through successive re-enactments, indirectly re-enacts with or without modification an enactment passed before that date.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/10" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/40/schedule/1/paragraph/3/10" id="schedule-1-paragraph-3-10"><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this paragraph, “<Term id="term-enactment">enactment</Term>” does not include an enactment contained in an order, regulation or other instrument made under an Act.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/1/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/1/b" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-1-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>were specified in the third column of Schedule 1 to that Act.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/2" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Without prejudice to the generality of subsection (1) of section 15 of the 1974 Act (health and safety regulations), regulations under that section may repeal or modify any of the provisions mentioned in sub-paragraph (1) above.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1995/45/schedule/4/paragraph/10/3" id="schedule-4-paragraph-10-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Nothing in sub-paragraph (1) above shall affect the operation of section 18 of the 1974 Act (enforcement of relevant statutory provisions) in relation to any time before such day as the Secretary of State may by order made by statutory instrument appoint, and different days may be appointed for different purposes.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/4/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/4/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/4/2/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-4-2-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the words from the beginning to “Chapter) or”                     United Kingdom waters
                  ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

NumberOfProvisions="6" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." id="schedule-1" RestrictStartDate="1997-03-23"><Number>SCHEDULE 1</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Amendments of Merchant Shipping Act 1995 relating to inspection and detention of ships</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/crossheading/enforcing-detention-of-ships" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/crossheading/enforcing-detention-of-ships" NumberOfProvisions="1" RestrictStartDate="1997-03-23" id="schedule-1-crossheading-enforcing-detention-of-ships"><Title> Enforcing detention of ships</Title><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5" RestrictStartDate="1997-03-23" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P1para><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/1" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/1" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-1"><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Section 284 of the 1995 Act (enforcing detention of ship) is amended as follows.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/2" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-2"><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (1), for paragraph (b) there is substituted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>any officer of a Minister of the Crown or Northern Ireland department who is authorised by the Secretary of State, either generally or in a particular case, to exercise powers under this section,</Text></P3para></P3></BlockAmendment><AppendText>.</AppendText></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/3" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/3" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-3"><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>After subsection (1) there is inserted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>1A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A notice of detention may—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>include a direction that the ship—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>must remain in a particular place, or</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>must be moved to a particular anchorage or berth, and</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>if it includes such a direction, may specify circumstances relating to safety or the prevention of pollution in which the master may move his ship from that place, anchorage or berth.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/4" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For subsection (2) there is substituted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="primary" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>If a ship as respects which notice of detention has been served on the master proceeds to sea, otherwise than in accordance with such a notice, before it is released by a competent authority, the master of the ship shall be guilty of an offence.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>If a ship as respects which notice of detention has been served on the master fails to comply with a direction given under subsection (1A)(a) above, the master of the ship shall be guilty of an offence.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2B</Pnumber><P2para><Text>A person guilty of an offence under subsection (2) or (2A) above shall be liable—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>on summary conviction, to a fine not exceeding £50,000;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>on conviction on indictment, to a fine.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/5" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/5" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-5"><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (3), after “subsection (2)” there is inserted <InlineAmendment>“
                    or (2A)
                  ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-6"><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In subsection (4)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-6-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>after “subsection (2) above” there is inserted <InlineAmendment>“
                        or failing to comply with a direction given under subsection (1A)(a) above
                      ”</InlineAmendment>,</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-6-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for “takes to sea” there is substituted <InlineAmendment>“
                        carries away without his consent
                      ”</InlineAmendment>, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6/c" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/6/c" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-6-c"><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in paragraph (i), for “taken to sea” there is substituted <InlineAmendment>“
                        carried away
                      ”</InlineAmendment>.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-7"><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Any reference to section 284 of the 1995 Act, or to provisions of that section—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-7-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in any safety regulations within the meaning of the 1995 Act made before commencement,</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-7-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in any Order in Council having effect under section 128 or 129 of the 1995 Act and made before commencement, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7/c" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/7/c" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-7-c"><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in any regulations having effect under such an Order and made before commencement,</Text></P3para></P3><Text>shall have effect as a reference to section 284, or those provisions, as amended by this paragraph.</Text></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/8" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/5/8" id="schedule-1-paragraph-5-8"><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (7) above “<Term id="term-commencement">commencement</Term>” means the commencement of this paragraph.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

                          ”</InlineAmendment>, and</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/3/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/3/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-6-3-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>after that sub-paragraph there is inserted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>4A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>The power of detention conferred by sub-paragraph (4) above is not exercisable in relation to a qualifying foreign ship while the ship is exercising—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the right of innocent passage, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the right of transit passage through straits used for international navigation.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/4" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/4" id="schedule-1-paragraph-6-4"><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In paragraph 17 (inspection)—</Text><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/4/a" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/4/a" id="schedule-1-paragraph-6-4-a"><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>in sub-paragraphs (1) and (2), for “any port in the United Kingdom” there is substituted <InlineAmendment>“
                        United Kingdom waters
                      ”</InlineAmendment>, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/4/b" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/1/paragraph/6/4/b" id="schedule-1-paragraph-6-4-b"><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>after sub-paragraph (2) there is inserted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="unknown" Format="default"><P2><Pnumber>2A</Pnumber><P2para><Text>No power of inspection conferred by sub-paragraph (1) or (2) above is exercisable in relation to a qualifying foreign ship while the ship is exercising—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the right of innocent passage, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the right of transit passage through straits used for international navigation.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></BlockAmendment></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock></ScheduleBody></Schedule></Schedules></Primary></Legislation>

xmls: <Legislation xmlns="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28" NumberOfProvisions="102" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/namespaces/legislation http://www.legislation.gov.uk/schema/legislation.xsd" SchemaVersion="1.0" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2015-03-12"><Primary><Schedules RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I." RestrictStartDate="2011-04-22"><Title> SCHEDULES</Title><Schedule DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/2" NumberOfProvisions="19" id="schedule-2" RestrictStartDate="2011-04-22"><Number>SCHEDULE 2</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Funding of maritime services</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><P1 DocumentURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/2/paragraph/2" IdURI="http://www.legislation.gov.uk/id/ukpga/1997/28/schedule/2/paragraph/2" RestrictStartDate="2011-04-22" id="schedule-2-paragraph-2" RestrictExtent="E+W+S+N.I."><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P1para><Text>After Schedule 11 to the 1995 Act there is inserted—</Text><BlockAmendment TargetClass="unknown" TargetSubClass="unknown" Context="main" Format="default"><Schedule><Number>Schedule 11A</Number><TitleBlock><Title> Funding of maritime services</Title></TitleBlock><ScheduleBody><Pblock><Title> Interpretation</Title><P1><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P1para><Text>In this Schedule—</Text><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition"><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>general light dues</Term>” and “<Term>general lighthouse authority</Term>” have the same meaning as in Part VIII of this Act;</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>prescribe</Term>” means prescribe by regulations.</Text></Para></ListItem></UnorderedList></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Charges in respect of maritime matters</Title><P1><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may make provision imposing charges for the purpose of recovering the whole or a part of the costs incurred by the Secretary of State in connection with his maritime functions.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (1) above “<Term>maritime functions</Term>” means—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>functions conferred by or under any provision of this Act apart from Part II or Part VIII,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>functions under any international agreement relating to—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the safety of ships,</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>the prevention of pollution from ships, or</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>iii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>living and working conditions on board ships, and</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>other functions relating to the promotion of the safety of ships.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Charges relating to expenses payable out of General Lighthouse Fund</Title><P1><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>If—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>any  <Substitution ChangeId="key-ca7c5d-1525167558939" CommentaryRef="key-ca7c5d">EU</Substitution>  obligation, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>any international agreement made between any three or more countries including the Republic of Ireland and ratified by the United Kingdom,</Text></P3para></P3><Text>requires the United Kingdom to provide for any of the costs incurred by general lighthouse authorities in respect of lighthouses, buoys and beacons to be recovered otherwise than by means of the levying of general light dues in accordance with section 205 (as it has effect on the commencement of this Schedule), regulations under this Schedule may make provision imposing charges for the purposes of recovering all or any part of the costs required to be so recovered.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this paragraph “<Term>buoys and beacons</Term>” includes equipment which is intended as an aid to the navigation of ships and, subject to that, expressions used in this paragraph and in Part VIII of this Act have the same meaning as in that Part.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Ships in respect of which charges may be imposed</Title><P1><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may not require a charge to be paid except in respect of—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a ship which has entered a port in the United Kingdom,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a ship which is anchored off a port in the United Kingdom, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>a ship which is anchored within 500 metres of an installation which is in United Kingdom waters or a part of the sea specified by virtue of section 129(2)(b).</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Nothing in any regulations under this Schedule shall be construed as requiring a charge to be paid in respect of a qualifying foreign ship which is exercising—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the right of innocent passage, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the right of transit passage through straits used for international navigation,</Text></P3para></P3><Text>except to the extent that international law allows such a charge to be imposed.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subject to sub-paragraphs (1) and (2) above, the regulations may impose a charge in respect of such description of ship as may be prescribed.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>4</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In particular—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>regulations may impose a charge in respect of a ship even though no service has been provided or function exercised in the case of that ship; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>regulations may provide that no charge is imposed in respect of a ship which does not exceed a prescribed tonnage or does not exceed a prescribed length.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P2para><Text>For the purposes of sub-paragraph (1)(a) above, the circumstances in which a ship shall be regarded as entering a port in the United Kingdom include circumstances in which the ship enters any United Kingdom waters which are regulated or managed by a harbour authority.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In sub-paragraph (1)(c) above “<Term>installation</Term>” means an installation which—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>is an offshore installation within the meaning of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8633911"/>Mineral Workings (Offshore Installations) Act 1971; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>is to be taken to be an installation for the purposes of sections 21 to 23 of the <CommentaryRef Ref="c8633921"/>Petroleum Act 1987.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Persons by whom charges to be paid</Title><P1><Pnumber>5</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may not require a charge to be paid in respect of a ship by a person who is not—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the owner of the ship;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the person registered as the owner of the ship;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the operator of the ship;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the manager of the ship;</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>e</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the charterer of the ship; or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>f</Pnumber><P3para><Text>the agent of a person mentioned in any of paragraphs (a) to (e) above.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Subject to sub-paragraph (1) above, charges imposed by the regulations shall be payable by such persons as may be prescribed.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Amount of charges</Title><P1><Pnumber>6</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may impose a charge—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>of a fixed amount, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>of an amount determined in accordance with the regulations,</Text></P3para></P3><Text>and may impose different charges in relation to ships of different descriptions or in different circumstances.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may, in particular, impose in respect of a ship a charge whose amount depends on—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>whether action has been or is being taken with a view to—</Text><P4><Pnumber>i</Pnumber><P4para><Text>enforcing international shipping standards in the case of that ship, or</Text></P4para></P4><P4><Pnumber>ii</Pnumber><P4para><Text>preventing, reducing or minimising the effects of pollution from that ship; and</Text></P4para></P4></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>if any such action has been or is being so taken, the nature of the action.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>3</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may, in particular, impose in respect of a ship a charge whose amount depends on the tonnage or length of the ship.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Powers to require information</Title><P1><Pnumber>7</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may include provision requiring any relevant authority or any person who is or may be liable to pay charges under the regulations in respect of a ship, to provide any collecting authority with such information as the collecting authority may reasonably require for the purposes of the regulations.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>In this paragraph—</Text><UnorderedList Decoration="none" Class="Definition"><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>collecting authority</Term>” means—</Text></Para><OrderedList Type="alpha" Decoration="parens"><ListItem NumberOverride="a"><Para><Text>the Secretary of State,</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem NumberOverride="b"><Para><Text>a Departmental officer, and</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem NumberOverride="c"><Para><Text>a general lighthouse authority;</Text></Para></ListItem></OrderedList></ListItem><ListItem><Para><Text>“<Term>relevant authority</Term>” means—</Text></Para><OrderedList Type="alpha" Decoration="parens"><ListItem NumberOverride="a"><Para><Text>a harbour authority,</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem NumberOverride="b"><Para><Text>the Commissioners of Customs and Excise, and</Text></Para></ListItem><ListItem NumberOverride="c"><Para><Text>a conservancy authority.</Text></Para></ListItem></OrderedList></ListItem></UnorderedList></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Disclosure of information</Title><P1><Pnumber>8</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>No obligation as to secrecy or other restriction on the disclosure of information (whether imposed by statute or otherwise) shall prevent a Minister of the Crown or a Northern Ireland department from disclosing—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to the Secretary of State, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to a person appointed by the Secretary of State to collect charges under regulations made under this Schedule,</Text></P3para></P3><Text>information for the purpose of enabling or assisting the Secretary of State to perform his functions under the regulations.</Text></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Information obtained by any person by virtue of sub-paragraph (1) above shall not be disclosed by him to any other person except where the disclosure is made—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>to a person falling within sub-paragraph (1)(a) or (b) above, or</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the purposes of any legal proceedings arising out of the regulations.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Collection and recovery, etc.</Title><P1><Pnumber>9</Pnumber><P1para><P2><Pnumber>1</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may make provision—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>with respect to the collection and recovery of charges; and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for charges which fall due under the regulations but which are not paid to carry interest.</Text></P3para></P3></P2para></P2><P2><Pnumber>2</Pnumber><P2para><Text>Regulations made under this Schedule by virtue of sub-paragraph (1) above may in particular confer on general lighthouse authorities functions relating to the collection and recovery of charges.</Text></P2para></P2></P1para></P1><P1><Pnumber>10</Pnumber><P1para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may make provision for appeals against decisions that charges are due in respect of ships.</Text></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Distress</Title><P1><Pnumber>11</Pnumber><P1para><Text>Regulations under this Schedule may make provision in respect of England and Wales and Northern Ireland—</Text><P3><Pnumber>a</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for authorising distress to be levied on any ship in respect of which the owner or master has failed to pay charges due under the regulations, and on any goods, equipment or other thing belonging to, or on board, the ship,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the disposal of any ship, goods, equipment or other thing on which distress is levied in accordance with the regulations, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>for the imposition and recovery of costs, charges, expenses and fees in connection with anything done under regulations made by virtue of paragraph (a) or (b) above.</Text></P3para></P3></P1para></P1></Pblock><Pblock><Title>Further powers in relation to General Lighthouse Fund <Abbreviation Expansion="Et cetera" xml:lang="la">etc</Abbreviation></Title><P1><Pnumber>12</Pnumber><P1para><Text>If regulations under this Schedule make any provision by virtue of paragraph 3 above, regulations under this Schedule may out of money provided by Parliament,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>b</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provide for amounts which, apart from the regulations, would fall to be paid into the General Lighthouse Fund (other than general light dues levied in accordance with section 205) to be paid by the Secretary of State into the Consolidated Fund,</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>c</Pnumber><P3para><Text>provide for the payment out of money provided by Parliament into the General Lighthouse Fund of amounts representing the whole or part of any charges imposed by virtue of paragraph 3, and</Text></P3para></P3><P3><Pnumber>d</Pnumber><P3para><Text>make such amendments, repeals or other modifications of any of the provisions of this Act relating to the General Lighthouse Fund or general light dues as appear to the Secretary of State to be necessary or expedient in consequence of, or in connection with, the provision made by virtue of paragraph 3 above or paragraph (a), (b) or (c) above.</Text></P3para></P3></P1para></P1><P1><Pnumber>13</Pnumber><P1para><Text>If regulations under this Schedule make any provision by virtue of paragraph 9(2) above, regulations under this Schedule may also provide for the making by the Secretary of State to each general lighthouse authority out of money provided by Parliament of payments in SCHEDULESSCHEDULE 3 Provisions to be inserted as Schedule 5A to the Merchant Shipping Act 1995Section 14(2).Text of International Convention on Liability and Compensation for Damage in Connection with the Carriage of Hazardous and Noxious Substances by SeaThe States parties to the present Convention,Conscious of the dangers posed by the world-wide carriage by sea of hazardous and noxious substances,Convinced of the need to ensure that adequate, prompt and effective compensation is available to persons who suffer damage caused by incidents in connection with the carriage by sea of such substances,Desiring to adopt uniform international rules and procedures for determining questions of liability and compensation in respect of such damage,Considering that the economic consequences of damage caused by the carriage by sea of hazardous and noxious substances should be shared by the shipping industry and the cargo interests involved,Have agreed as follows:Chapter I GENERAL PROVISIONS Definitions<Emphasis>Article 1</Emphasis>

For the purposes of this Convention:

1. “Ship” means any seagoing vessel and seaborne craft, of any type whatsoever.

2. “Person” means any individual or partnership or any public or private body, whether corporate or not, including a State or any of its constituent subdivisions.

3. “Owner” means the person or persons registered as the owner of the ship or, in the absence of registration, the person or persons owning the ship. However, in the case of a ship owned by a State and operated by a company which in that State is registered as the ship’s operator, “owner” shall mean such company.

4. “Receiver” means either:(a) the person who physically receives contributing cargo discharged in the ports and terminals of a State Party; provided that if at the time of receipt the person who physically receives the cargo acts as an agent for another who is subject to the jurisdiction of any State Party, then the principal shall be deemed to be the receiver, if the agent discloses the principal to the HNS Fund; or(b) the person in the State Party who in accordance with the national law of that State Party is deemed to be the receiver of contributing cargo discharged in the ports and terminals of a State Party, provided that the total contributing cargo received according to such national law is substantially the same as that which would have been received under (a).

5. “Hazardous and noxious substances” (HNS) means:(a) any substances, materials and articles carried on board a ship as cargo, referred to in (i) to (vii) below:

(i) oils carried in bulk listed in appendix I of Annex I to the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships, 1973, as modified by the Protocol of 1978 relating thereto, as amended;

(ii) noxious liquid substances carried in bulk referred to in appendix II of Annex II to the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships, 1973, as modified by the Protocol of 1978 relating thereto, as amended, and those substances and mixtures provisionally categorized as falling in pollution category A, B, C or D in accordance with regulation 3(4) of the said Annex II;

(iii) dangerous liquid substances carried in bulk listed in chapter 17 of the International Code for the Construction and Equipment of Ships Carrying Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk, 1983, as amended, and the dangerous products for which the preliminary suitable conditions for the carriage have been prescribed by the Administration and port administrations involved in accordance with paragraph 1.1.3 of the Code;

(iv) dangerous, hazardous and harmful substances, materials and articles in packaged form covered by the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code, as amended;

(v) liquefied gases as listed in chapter 19 of the International Code for the Construction and Equipment of Ships Carrying Liquefied Gases in Bulk, 1983, as amended, and the products for which preliminary suitable conditions for the carriage have been prescribed by the Administration and port administrations involved in accordance with paragraph 1.1.6 of the Code;

(vi) liquid substances carried in bulk with a flashpoint not exceeding 60°C (measured by a closed cup test);

(vii) solid bulk materials possessing chemical hazards covered by appendix B of the Code of Safe Practice for Solid Bulk Cargoes, as amended, to the extent that these substances are also subject to the provisions of the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code when carried in packaged form; and(b) residues from the previous carriage in bulk of substances referred to in (a)(i) to (iii) and (v) to (vii) above.

6. “Damage” means:(a) loss of life or personal injury on board or outside the ship carrying the hazardous and noxious substances caused by those substances;(b) loss of or damage to property outside the ship carrying the hazardous and noxious substances caused by those substances;(c) loss or damage by contamination of the environment caused by the hazardous and noxious substances, provided that compensation for impairment of the environment other than loss of profit from such impairment shall be limited to costs of reasonable measures of reinstatement actually undertaken or to be undertaken; and(d) the costs of preventive measures and further loss or damage caused by preventive measures.

Where it is not reasonably possible to separate damage caused by the hazardous and noxious substances from that caused by other factors, all such damage shall be deemed to be caused by the hazardous and noxious substances except if, and to the extent that, the damage caused by other factors is damage of a type referred to in article 4, paragraph 3.

In this paragraph, “caused by those substances” means caused by the hazardous or noxious nature of the substances.

7. “Preventive measures” means any reasonable measures taken by any person after an incident has occurred to prevent or minimize damage.

8. “Incident” means any occurrence or series of occurrences having the same origin, which causes damage or creates a grave and imminent threat of causing damage.

9. “Carriage by sea” means the period from the time when the hazardous and noxious substances enter any part of the ship’s equipment, on loading, to the time they cease to be present in any part of the ship’s equipment, on discharge. If no ship’s equipment is used, the period begins and ends respectively when the hazardous and noxious substances cross the ship’s rail.

10. “Contributing cargo” means any hazardous and noxious substances which are carried by sea as cargo to a port or terminal in the territory of a State Party and discharged in that State. Cargo in transit which is transferred directly, or through a port or terminal, from one ship to another, either wholly or in part, in the course of carriage from the port or terminal of original loading to the port or terminal of final destination shall be considered as contributing cargo only in respect of receipt at the final destination.

11. The “HNS Fund” means the International Hazardous and Noxious Substances Fund established under article 13.

12. “Unit of account” means the Special Drawing Right as defined by the International Monetary Fund.

13. “State of the ship’s registry” means in relation to a registered ship the State of registration of the ship, and in relation to an unregistered ship the State whose flag the ship is entitled to fly.

14. “Terminal” means any site for the storage of hazardous and noxious substances received from waterborne transportation, including any facility situated off-shore and linked by pipeline or otherwise to such site.

15. “Director” means the Director of the HNS Fund.

16. “Organization” means the International Maritime Organization.

17. “Secretary-General” means the Secretary-General of the Organization.

 Annexes<Emphasis>Article 2</Emphasis>

The Annexes to this Convention shall constitute an integral part of this Convention.

 Scope of application<Emphasis>Article 3</Emphasis>

This Convention shall apply exclusively:(a) to any damage caused in the territory, including the territorial sea, of a State Party;(b) to damage by contamination of the environment caused in the exclusive economic zone of a State Party, established in accordance with international law, or, if a State Party has not established such a zone, in an area beyond and adjacent to the territorial sea of that State determined by that State in accordance with international law and extending not more than 200 nautical miles from the baselines from which the breadth of its territorial sea is measured;(c) to damage, other than damage by contamination of the environment, caused outside the territory, including the territorial sea, of any State, if this damage has been caused by a substance carried on board a ship registered in a State Party or, in the case of an unregistered ship, on board a ship entitled to fly the flag of a State Party; and(d) to preventive measures, wherever taken.

<Emphasis>Article 4</Emphasis>

1. This Convention shall apply to claims, other than claims arising out of any contract for the carriage of goods and passengers, for damage arising from the carriage of hazardous and noxious substances by sea.

2. This Convention shall not apply to the extent that its provisions are incompatible with those of the applicable law relating to workers’ compensation or social security schemes.

3. This Convention shall not apply:(a) to pollution damage as defined in the International Convention on Civil Liability for Oil Pollution Damage, 1969, as amended, whether or not compensation is payable in respect of it under that Convention; and(b) to damage caused by a radioactive material of class 7 either in the International Maritime Dangerous Goods Code, as amended, or in appendix B of the Code of Safe Practice for Solid Bulk Cargoes, as amended.

4. Except as provided in paragraph 5, the provisions of this Convention shall not apply to warships, naval auxiliary or other ships owned or operated by a State and used, for the time being, only on Government non-commercial service.

5. A State Party may decide to apply this Convention to its warships or other vessels described in paragraph 4, in which case it shall notify the Secretary-General thereof specifying the terms and conditions of such application.

6. With respect to ships owned by a State Party and used for commercial purposes, each State shall be subject to suit in the jurisdictions set forth in article 38 and shall waive all defences based on its status as a sovereign State.

<Emphasis>Article 5</Emphasis>

1. A State may, at the time of ratification, acceptance, approval of, or accession to, this Convention, or any time thereafter, declare that this Convention does not apply to ships:(a) which do not exceed 200 gross tonnage; and(b) which carry hazardous and noxious substances only in packaged form; and(c) while they are engaged on voyages between ports or facilities of that State.

2. Where two neighbouring States agree that this Convention does not apply also to ships which are covered by paragraph 1(a) and (b) while engaged on voyages between ports or facilities of those States, the States concerned may declare that the exclusion from the application of this Convention declared under paragraph 1 covers also ships referred to in this paragraph.

3. Any State which has made the declaration under paragraph 1 or 2 may withdraw such declaration at any time.

4. A declaration made under paragraph 1 or 2, and the withdrawal of the declaration made under paragraph 3, shall be deposited with the Secretary-General who shall, after the entry into force of this Convention, communicate it to the Director.

5. Where a State has made a declaration under paragraph 1 or 2 and has not withdrawn it, hazardous and noxious substances carried on board ships covered by that paragraph shall not be considered to be contributing cargo for the purpose of application of articles 18, 20, article 21, paragraph 5 and article 43.

6. The HNS Fund is not liable to pay compensation for damage caused by substances carried by a ship to which the Convention does not apply pursuant to a declaration made under paragraph 1 or 2, to the extent that:(a) the damage as defined in article 1, paragraph 6(a), (b) or (c) was caused in:(i) the territory, including the territorial sea, of the State which has made the declaration, or in the case of neighbouring States which have made a declaration under paragraph 2, of either of them; or(ii) the exclusive economic zone, or area mentioned in article 3(b), of the State or States referred to in (i);(b) the damage includes measures taken to prevent or minimize such damage.

 Duties of State Parties<Emphasis>Article 6</Emphasis>

Each State Party shall ensure that any obligation arising under this Convention is fulfilled and shall take appropriate measures under its law including the imposing of sanctions as it may deem necessary, with a view to the effective execution of any such obligation.

Chapter II LIABILITY Liability of the owner<Emphasis>Article 7</Emphasis>

1. Except as provided in paragraphs 2 and 3, the owner at the time of an incident shall be liable for damage caused by any hazardous and noxious substances in connection with their carriage by sea on board the ship, provided that if an incident consists of a series of occurrences having the same origin the liability shall attach to the owner at the time of the first of such occurrences.

2. No liability shall attach to the owner if the owner proves that:(a) the damage resulted from an act of war, hostilities, civil war, insurrection or a natural phenomenon of an exceptional, inevitable and irresistible character; or(b) the damage was wholly caused by an act or omission done with the intent to cause damage by a third party; or(c) the damage was wholly caused by the negligence or other wrongful act of any Government or other authority responsible for the maintenance of lights or other navigational aids in the exercise of that function; or(d) the failure of the shipper or any other person to furnish information concerning the hazardous and noxious nature of the substances shipped either(i) has caused the damage, wholly or partly; or(ii) has led the owner not to obtain insurance in accordance with article 12;

provided that neither the owner nor its servants or agents knew or ought reasonably to have known of the hazardous and noxious nature of the substances shipped.

3. If the owner proves that the damage resulted wholly or partly either from an act or omission done with intent to cause damage by the person who suffered the damage or from the negligence of that person, the owner may be exonerated wholly or partially from liability to such person.

4. No claim for compensation for damage shall be made against the owner otherwise than in accordance with this Convention.

5. Subject to paragraph 6, no claim for compensation for damage under this Convention or otherwise may be made against:(a) the servants or agents of the owner or the members of the crew;(b) the pilot or any other person who, without being a member of the crew, performs services for the ship;(c) any charterer (howsoever described, including a bareboat charterer), manager or operator of the ship;(d) any person performing salvage operations with the consent of the owner or on the instructions of a competent public authority;(e) any person taking preventive measures; and(f) the servants or agents of persons mentioned in (c), (d) and (e);

unless the damage resulted from their personal act or omission, committed with the intent to cause such damage, or recklessly and with knowledge that such damage would probably result.

6. Nothing in this Convention shall prejudice any existing right of recourse of the owner against any third party, including, but not limited to, the shipper or the receiver of the substance causing the damage, or the persons indicated in paragraph 5.

 Incidents involving two or more ships<Emphasis>Article 8</Emphasis>

1. Whenever damage has resulted from an incident involving two or more ships each of which is carrying hazardous and noxious substances, each owner, unless exonerated under article 7, shall be liable for the damage. The owners shall be jointly and severally liable for all such damage which is not reasonably separable.

2. However, owners shall be entitled to the limits of liability applicable to each of them under article 9.

3. Nothing in this article shall prejudice any right of recourse of an owner against any other owner.

 Limitation of liability<Emphasis>Article 9</Emphasis>

1. The owner of a ship shall be entitled to limit liability under this Convention in respect of any one incident to an aggregate amount calculated as follows:(a) 10 million units of account for a ship not exceeding 2,000 units of tonnage; and(b) for a ship with a tonnage in excess thereof, the following amount in addition to that mentioned in (a):for each unit of tonnage from 2,001 to 50,000 units of tonnage, 1,500 units of account

for each unit of tonnage in excess of 50,000 units of tonnage, 360 units of account

provided, however, that this aggregate amount shall not in any event exceed 100 million units of account.

2. The owner shall not be entitled to limit liability under this Convention if it is proved that the damage resulted from the personal act or omission of the owner, committed with the intent to cause such damage, or recklessly and with knowledge that such damage would probably result.

3. The owner shall, for the purpose of benefitting from the limitation provided for in paragraph 1, constitute a fund for the total sum representing the limit of liability established in accordance with paragraph 1 with the court or other competent authority of any one of the States Parties in which action is brought under article 38 or, if no action is brought, with any court or other competent authority in any one of the States Parties in which an action can be brought under article 38. The fund can be constituted either by depositing the sum or by producing a bank guarantee or other guarantee, acceptable under the law of the State Party where the fund is constituted, and considered to be adequate by the court or other competent authority.

4. Subject to the provisions of article 11, the fund shall be distributed among the claimants in proportion to the amounts of their established claims.

5. If before the fund is distributed the owner or any of the servants or agents of the owner or any person providing to the owner insurance or other financial security has as a result of the incident in question, paid compensation for damage, such person shall, up to the amount that person has paid, acquire by subrogation the rights which the person so compensated would have enjoyed under this Convention.

6. The right of subrogation provided for in paragraph 5 may also be exercised by a person other than those mentioned therein in respect of any amount of compensation for damage which such person may have paid but only to the extent that such subrogation is permitted under the applicable national law.

7. Where owners or other persons establish that they may be compelled to pay at a later date in whole or in part any such amount of compensation, with regard to which the right of subrogation would have been enjoyed under paragraphs 5 or 6 had the compensation been paid before the fund was distributed, the court or other competent authority of the State where the fund has been constituted may order that a sufficient sum shall be provisionally set aside to enable such person at such later date to enforce the claim against the fund.
